title: The 2026–2027 dental convention calendar
dek: From New York in November to Orlando in June, here is when and where America's major dental meetings happen next, as listed by their organizers.

body.p: Every year, tens of thousands of dentists, hygienists, assistants and lab technicians leave their offices for a few days to sit in lectures, practice on models and walk exhibit halls full of new equipment. Those meetings are where much of the profession's continuing education happens. They are also where a lot of the tools you later see in the chair are first shown to the people who will use them.
Here is the coming season in date order, as each organizer currently lists it. Dates change, so treat the official sites as the final word.

ul: Greater New York Dental Meeting: November 27 to December 1, 2026, Javits Center, New York City. Exhibits open November 29.
Yankee Dental Congress: January 28 to 30, 2027, Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center, Boston.
Chicago Midwinter Meeting: February 25 to 27, 2027, McCormick Place West, Chicago.
Hinman Dental Meeting: March 18 to 20, 2027, Georgia World Congress Center, Atlanta.
AACD Scientific Session: March 31 to April 3, 2027, Hollywood, Florida.
Florida Dental Convention: June 24 to 26, 2027, Gaylord Palms Resort & Convention Center, Orlando area.
ADA SmileCon: no next edition announced. The ADA ended the SmileCon brand and says its annual meeting is paused, apart from its House of Delegates, until further notice.

body.p: The big regional meetings in New York, Boston, Chicago and Atlanta are broad. They teach the whole dental team, from implants and orthodontics to infection control and office management, and they put hundreds of exhibitors on one floor. The Florida convention plays a similar role for the state. The AACD meeting is narrower and more focused: it is built around esthetic and restorative dentistry, the core of cosmetic work.
The ADA's national meeting is the outlier this season. After years of lower attendance and rising costs, the association stopped holding SmileCon and has not named a successor date.

Technology does not walk into a practice on its own. Digital scanners, chairside milling, 3D printing and AI-assisted imaging spread because dentists see them, try them and take courses on them. Techniques spread the same way. A new approach to smile design or a better bonding workflow usually reaches your mouth after it has been taught, debated and practiced at meetings like these.

Attendance alone does not make anyone a better dentist. What matters is what they learned and whether they kept practicing it. Still, continuing education is one of the clearest signals of a dentist who keeps up.

body.h: What to ask at your consultation

ul: What continuing education have you taken recently in the treatment you are recommending?
Which tools in your office are new in the last few years, and why did you choose them?
How do you decide whether a new technique is proven enough to use on patients?

body.p: Good answers are specific. A dentist who can explain why they adopted something, and why they skipped something else, is showing you judgment, not just a shopping list.

title: Greater New York Dental Meeting: the season opener in Manhattan
dek: The Greater New York Dental Meeting returns to the Javits Center November 27 to December 1, 2026, with exhibits open November 29 to December 1.

body.p: The Greater New York Dental Meeting is one of the largest gatherings of dental professionals in the country, and it opens the convention season each year just after Thanksgiving. The 2026 meeting runs Friday, November 27 through Tuesday, December 1, at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center in Manhattan. The exhibit floor is open Sunday, November 29 through Tuesday, December 1.

body.h: Who runs it and how big it is

body.p: The meeting is sponsored by two local organizations, the New York County and Second District Dental Societies, and run with the help of volunteers from both. Organizers report that the 2025 meeting drew more than 30,000 registrations, including roughly 12,000 dentists, along with hygienists and assistants, from well over 100 countries. They also report more than 450 technical exhibits that year.

One detail sets it apart. The organizers say it is the only major dental meeting with no pre-registration fee, which helps explain the crowd. The next edition after 2026 is already on the calendar: November 26 to 30, 2027.

body.h: What dentists go there to learn

body.p: The education program mixes full-day and half-day seminars with hands-on workshops, where dentists practice techniques on models rather than just watching slides. The 2026 program adds specialty tracks in areas such as implants, orthodontics, pediatric dentistry and dental lab education. Office staff can attend as well, which matters because modern cosmetic work depends on the whole team, not only the dentist.

The exhibit floor is the other half of the meeting. The organizers describe it as a place to touch, use and compare the newest materials and technology in dentistry. In practice, that is where many dentists first get their hands on equipment like intraoral scanners, imaging systems and new restorative materials before deciding whether to bring them home.

body.h: Why it matters in your chair

body.p: A meeting this size is a marketplace of ideas. Not every product on the floor is a breakthrough, and not every lecture changes practice. But when a technique or tool becomes common in offices a year or two later, it very often passed through rooms like these first.

For a patient, the useful takeaway is simple. Ask your dentist how they keep their training current. A thoughtful answer names a specific course or skill, explains why it matters for your treatment, and admits when a new tool is still unproven. Continuing education is not a guarantee of good work. It is a sign of a dentist who keeps checking their own.

title: Chicago Midwinter Meeting: a February tradition at McCormick Place
dek: The Chicago Dental Society's Midwinter Meeting is set for February 25 to 27, 2027, at McCormick Place West in Chicago.

body.p: The Chicago Midwinter Meeting is one of the long-running anchors of the American dental calendar. The Chicago Dental Society lists the 2027 meeting for February 25 to 27, 2027, at McCormick Place West, 2301 S. Indiana Avenue, in Chicago. Three days, one convention center, and a city full of dental professionals in the coldest part of the year.

The meeting is organized by the Chicago Dental Society, which says it has been delivering programs for its members for more than 160 years and describes itself as one of the largest local dental societies in the United States. The Midwinter Meeting is its signature event, bringing together, in the society's words, a dental community from near and far.

The format is the classic one. There is a continuing education program with lectures and courses for dentists and their teams, and an exhibit hall that the society says will feature the latest dental innovations from hundreds of exhibitors. Evenings fill with receptions and events, which is less trivial than it sounds. A great deal of practical knowledge moves between dentists in hallway conversations about what worked and what did not.

The society does not publish a single theme for the hall, and its pages do not list which products will appear in 2027. Broadly, large exhibit floors at meetings like this are where dentists compare digital scanners, imaging, 3D printers, milling units, restorative materials and practice software side by side, and talk to the companies that make them.

Dental technology changes faster than most people expect. A dentist who trained fifteen years ago may now plan veneers on a screen, take impressions with a scanner instead of trays of putty, or use software to preview a smile before any tooth is touched. Those shifts happen one practice at a time, and meetings like Midwinter are part of how they happen.
None of that means a newer tool is automatically better for you. Good dentistry is judgment first and equipment second. The useful questions at a consultation are practical ones:

ul: What training have you had in this procedure in the last few years?
Is this tool or material well established, or still new?
What would you do differently if you were treating your own teeth?

body.p: A dentist who answers plainly, without hype, is usually a dentist who learned more than how to buy something at a trade show.

title: Yankee Dental Congress: New England's January meeting
dek: Yankee Dental Congress, presented by the Massachusetts Dental Society, returns to Boston January 28 to 30, 2027, with esthetic and technology tracks.

body.p: Yankee Dental Congress is New England's big dental meeting, held in Boston every January. The 2027 edition runs January 28 to 30, 2027, at the Thomas M. Menino Convention & Exhibition Center in Boston. Registration and housing opened in early October 2026.

Yankee is sponsored by the Massachusetts Dental Society, in cooperation with the dental associations of Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Vermont. The organizers describe it as the largest gathering of dental professionals in the region and say it has been running for more than 50 years. Its audience is the whole dental team: dentists, hygienists, assistants, office managers and students.

Like other large meetings, Yankee pairs a continuing education program with an exhibit floor of dental technology and services. What is useful for patients is that its 2027 program publishes clear tracks, so you can see what dentists are being taught.

The Esthetic Track is a three-course program on esthetic and restorative dentistry. The organizers list courses on turning diagnostic wax-ups into finished restorations with input from master ceramists, on treating a gummy smile with Botox, and on facially driven treatment planning that runs from digital design to the final restoration. That last idea is the heart of modern smile design: start with the face, then design the teeth.

The Technology Track covers artificial intelligence in dentistry, including its effects on clinical care, operations and ethics, and a full day on restorative technologies and evidence-based workflows. There is also continuing education on the exhibit floor itself, so dentists can learn and look at equipment in the same afternoon.

Notice the theme in those course titles. The emphasis is on predictable results, team communication and evidence. That is a healthier message than any single gadget. A scanner or an AI tool is only as good as the planning and judgment of the person using it.

If you are considering veneers or other cosmetic work, it is fair to ask how your dentist plans a smile. Do they design from your face and lips? Do they show you a preview before treatment? Who makes the restorations, and how do they communicate with that lab? Dentists who take courses like these should be able to walk you through the process in plain language.

title: Hinman Dental Meeting: Atlanta's century-old classroom
dek: The Hinman Dental Society's 114th annual meeting is set for March 18 to 20, 2027, at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta.

body.p: The Hinman Dental Meeting has been running in Atlanta since 1912. The 2027 edition, which the organizers call the 114th annual meeting, runs March 18 to 20, 2027, at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta.

The meeting is run by the Hinman Dental Society, a nonprofit of more than 800 dentists, mostly in metro Atlanta. The society was founded in 1911 and named for the Atlanta dentist who started it. The first meeting followed in 1912, and the society describes it as a clinic strictly for serious professional education. Today it says excess revenue from the meeting funds scholarships.

The meeting has grown a long way from its early classes. The society reports that more than 12,000 dentists, hygienists, assistants and office staff attend each year, from Georgia, the Southeast, across the country and abroad.

Continuing education is the core. The society describes peer-reviewed courses and hands-on technical training for the whole team, from general dentists and specialists to hygienists, lab technicians and students. Hands-on matters. Watching a lecture about a bonding technique is useful. Practicing it under supervision is how skill actually changes.

The exhibit hall started in 1942 with 14 booths. The society now describes a cutting-edge trade show featuring the latest dental technology and live learning demonstrations, so dentists can see tools working rather than just reading about them. The organizers do not list specific products or exhibitors for 2027.

A meeting with this kind of history is a reminder that dentistry has always advanced through teaching. The tools change: impression trays give way to digital scanners, hand-carved models to 3D-printed ones, film X-rays to digital imaging read with the help of software. The method of spreading good practice stays the same. Dentists learn from other dentists, try new things carefully and bring them home.

For patients, that suggests two good questions. First, how does your dentist keep their skills current, and in which areas? Second, when they adopt something new, how do they decide it is ready? You are not looking for the newest office. You are looking for a dentist who learns steadily and changes their methods for good reasons.

title: AACD Scientific Session: where cosmetic dentistry talks shop
dek: The American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry holds its 2027 Scientific Session March 31 to April 3 in Hollywood, Florida.

body.p: Most big dental meetings cover everything. The AACD Scientific Session is built around one subject: esthetic and restorative dentistry, the work behind veneers, bonding, crowns and smile design. The 2027 meeting runs March 31 to April 3, 2027, at the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort in Hollywood, Florida, a short drive from Miami.

The meeting is organized by the American Academy of Cosmetic Dentistry, a professional organization devoted to cosmetic dentistry. According to the conference site, attendees must be AACD members to register. That makes it smaller and more specialized than the giant regional shows, and more of a working conference for people already invested in cosmetic dentistry.

The AACD describes general sessions designed to expand clinical expertise, open lectures, and hands-on workshops, which are limited and require registration. Its 2027 materials highlight education across esthetics, restorative workflows, digital innovation and practice growth.

There is also an exhibitor floor that the academy describes as showcasing the latest innovations in dental technology, materials and services. For a cosmetic meeting, that typically means the things that shape how a smile is designed and made: ceramics and composites, shade-matching and photography, digital design software, scanners and the lab workflows that connect the dentist to the ceramist.

body.h: Why it matters to someone considering veneers

body.p: Cosmetic dentistry is not a separate dental specialty. Any licensed dentist can offer veneers. That is exactly why focused education matters. A meeting like this is where dentists who want to do cosmetic work well study proportion, color, translucency, gum health and the details that separate a natural result from an obvious one.
Attending a meeting does not prove skill, and membership is not the same as a credential earned through examination. So ask specific questions:

ul: How much of your practice is cosmetic work like mine?
What cosmetic training have you completed recently?
Can I see before-and-after photos of your own cases, similar to mine?
Will I see a preview or trial of my new smile before anything is final?

body.p: A confident cosmetic dentist welcomes those questions. The answers will tell you more than any logo on the wall.

title: Florida Dental Convention: the state's meeting, every June
dek: The Florida Dental Association's convention returns to the Gaylord Palms in the Orlando area June 24 to 26, 2027, with 150-plus CE courses.

body.p: The Florida Dental Convention is the Florida Dental Association's annual meeting, the state's main gathering for dentists and their teams. The next edition runs June 24 to 26, 2027, at the Gaylord Palms Resort & Convention Center in Kissimmee, in the Orlando area. The association has already listed future June dates at the same venue through 2031.

The convention is run by the Florida Dental Association through its Committee on Conventions and Continuing Education. That makes it different from a commercial trade show. It is organized by the professional association for Florida dentists, with education built around what dentists in the state need, including hours that count toward license renewal.

The association describes three days of education and buying opportunities for the entire dental team. For 2027 it advertises more than 150 continuing education courses for dental professionals and more than 20 CE hours available for licensure. Florida dentists, like dentists in every state, must complete continuing education to keep their licenses, and a meeting like this is one efficient way to do it.

The exhibit hall is large. The association lists more than 350 vendors showcasing the latest tech and trends. It does not name specific products, but halls like this are where Florida dentists typically compare scanners, imaging, 3D printing, restorative materials and practice software, and where labs and manufacturers meet the dentists who buy from them. The organizers also lean into the social side, describing the event as not your average dental meeting.

If you see a dentist in Florida, there is a good chance they have walked this floor or taken a course here. That makes it a useful lens on what is changing in local practices. When a new scanner, material or digital design tool shows up in your dentist's office, it often arrived by way of meetings like this one.

Continuing education is a requirement, not a distinction, so the useful question is not whether your dentist took courses. It is which ones. Ask what they have studied recently that relates to your treatment, how it changed the way they work, and how they decide when a new tool is ready for patients. Specific answers are a good sign.

title: ADA SmileCon: the national meeting that went quiet
dek: The ADA ended SmileCon after 2025 and says its annual meeting is paused until further notice. Next dates: to be announced.

body.p: For years, the American Dental Association's national meeting was a fixture of the fall calendar, most recently under the name SmileCon. Today there is no next edition to point to. Dates are to be announced, and the ADA has not committed to a future meeting.

In May 2025 the ADA announced it would end SmileCon. The association said the meeting had drawn positive feedback, but attendance never rebounded to pre-pandemic levels, and the rising cost of holding events was also a factor. The last edition under the SmileCon name was scheduled for October 23 to 25, 2025, in Washington, D.C. The ADA said a planned 2026 SmileCon in Indianapolis would not move forward.

The picture since then has been mixed. The ADA's SmileCon page lists an ADA 2026 Scientific Session, formerly known as SmileCon, for October 8 to 10, 2026, in Indianapolis. Its future meetings page now says the association has paused its annual meeting, apart from its House of Delegates, until further notice, after a bylaw change removed the requirement to hold an annual scientific session. The next House of Delegates is listed for October 29 to November 1, 2027, in Denver, but that is a governance meeting, not a convention.

As a national event run by the ADA, the meeting offered what the big regional shows do: continuing education for the whole dental team and an exhibit hall where companies showed new equipment and materials. Its draw was breadth. It was the one meeting not tied to a single city or region.

Very little changes in your chair. Dentists did not stop learning when SmileCon ended. They still have the large regional meetings in New York, Boston, Chicago and Atlanta, state meetings like Florida's, specialty meetings such as the AACD's for cosmetic work, and a great deal of online and hands-on coursework. New tools like digital scanners, 3D printing and AI-assisted imaging still reach practices through those channels.

The lesson is about where to look. A convention badge was never the point. What matters is whether your dentist keeps learning in the areas that affect your care. At a consultation, ask what training they have taken recently for the treatment you want, and how they decide when a new technique is ready to use.
We will update this page if the ADA announces a new national meeting.
